Most lawn mowers produce between 85 and 100 decibels, right at or above the threshold where hearing damage begins. And it's not just lawn mowers. Leaf blowers, chainsaws, and weed eaters can push noise levels even higher, exposing anyone in close earshot to long-term hearing loss risk. Traditional foam earplugs protect your hearing, but they also block everything else. No music. No podcasts. No phone calls. No spatial or situational awareness. That's where Bluetooth hearing protection for mowing changes everything. How Loud Is Lawn Care Equipment? Most people underestimate how loud yard equipment actually is — or what constitutes hazardous noise. Understanding the sound levels produced is a great first step toward protecting your hearing.
